html:
The Burundian unrest began in April 2015 when President Pierre Nkurunziza said he would run for a third term, which opponents said broke the limit set by the Arusha Accords.

Protests filled the streets of Bujumbura, and in May army officers tried a coup while he was abroad. It failed, and the government cracked down hard, with killings, disappearances and closed radio stations. Nkurunziza won the July election.

Hundreds of thousands fled to Tanzania, Rwanda and other neighbours. In 2017 Burundi became the first country to leave the International Criminal Court. Nkurunziza did not stand in 2020 and died that year, after the ruling party had changed the constitution. The crisis left the country among the poorest in the world.
sum: The Burundian unrest began in April 2015 when President Pierre Nkurunziza said he would run for a third term, which opponents said broke the limit set by the Arusha Accords.
